title: Kestrel and the Orbit
premise: Marguerite Hartwell is a clone of a murdered shipping magnate, running cargo on the Kestrel along the silent route between the Core worlds and the abandoned colonies. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Marguerite and their ragtag crew discover it's a beacon from the relay at the edge of dead space — and that the original Hartwell was killed because she found it first. Racing a closing jump window, they uncover that the corporation funding their voyage engineered both the murder and the signal to bury a colony of memory-archivists who hold proof of the board's oldest crime. In the end, Marguerite must choose between erasing the archive (and the original's memories inside it) or broadcasting it and losing everything the name Hartwell still owns; they broadcast, severing themselves from the inheritance but binding the crew into the family they chose.
about_author: Elodie Oyelaran is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years scheduling freight runs between stations that no longer exchanged mail. She writes science fiction about people who keep promises across distances that shouldn't allow them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine haul through the silent corridor between Meridian and Ceres Verge establishes the Kestrel's crew: engineer Sefa, pilot twins Idris and Noor, and ship-mind ORBIT. Marguerite reflects on being a clone who inherited a murder case no one solved. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: Cargo of Names
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Loading at Ceres Verge, the crew takes on an odd last-minute passenger: Dr. Amara Voss, a linguist studying dead languages, who pays triple for passage toward dead space. Marguerite distrusts her. Beat: unease disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: ORBIT's POV. The ship intercepts a repeating distress transmission in Ashkari, a language extinct two centuries. Voss confirms it's genuine and old-yet-live. The jump window to reach its source closes in nine days. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Inheritance Clauses
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reviewing the original Hartwell's sealed files to justify the detour, Marguerite finds a redacted reference to 'the Ashkari relay' dated three days before the murder. Someone aboard may be reporting to the estate's trustees. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The vote to chase the signal nearly splits the crew; Noor wants the safe contract, Idris argues the window won't reopen for a year. They commit. First sabotage: a fuel line fails in a way ORBIT can't explain. Beat: fragile unity under strain.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She reveals she decoded fragments of the original Hartwell's private correspondence; the magnate had located the relay and was silenced for it. Voss admits she didn't book passage by chance. Beat: betrayal reframed as desperate honesty.

chapters.title: The Trustee
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A corporate cutter shadows them; aboard is Executor Calloway, trustee of the Hartwell estate, ordering them to turn back. He hints he knows what Marguerite is — and that clones have no legal standing to refuse. Beat: power flexing its paperwork.

chapters.title: Dead Space Edge
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Kestrel crosses into dead space where comms die and ORBIT's sensors go half-blind. The crew runs on analog discipline and trust. Marguerite begins experiencing flashes of the original's memories — implanted, not inherited. Beat: intimacy with a ghost.

chapters.title: Memory Bleed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The flashes intensify: the original's last day, a handshake, a corridor, someone saying 'the children are still singing.' Marguerite confides in Voss, who identifies the phrase as Ashkari. Beat: grief for a life that wasn't yours.

chapters.title: Calloway Boards
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The cutter forces a docking under salvage law. Calloway searches the ship, confiscates Voss's decodes, and offers Marguerite a deal: abandon the relay, receive full legal personhood. Marguerite stalls. Beat: temptation priced exactly right.

chapters.title: The Twins' Gambit
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The twins fake a reactor failure to break free of the cutter during the next jump window. It works, barely; ORBIT burns out a secondary core covering their escape. Beat: family forged in reckless competence.

chapters.title: Songs from the Dark
chapters.summary: ORBIT's POV. Approaching the relay, they pick up audio: children's voices singing Ashkari lullabies, live, not archived. The extinct language isn't extinct. The distress call was a trap — or a plea. Beat: hope arriving like vertigo.

chapters.title: The Archive Colony
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. They dock at the relay-station Halcyon Reach: descendants of the Ashkari diaspora who preserve memories as living archives, including recordings the original Hartwell smuggled out — proof the Hartwell Corporation founded itself on a massacre. Beat: the case solves itself, horribly.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The colony's Keeper shows Marguerite the original's deposited memories: she came to atone, not to profit, and asked that any clone of hers be told the truth. Marguerite realizes the flashes were a message sent forward. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Calloway's cutter arrives with a corporate interdiction fleet behind it; the jump window home closes in thirty hours. Broadcast the archive and every Hartwell asset — including the Kestrel's registry — is seized. Beat: the walls drawing in.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV (first antagonist chapter). He isn't a monster; he genuinely believes burying the massacre saved millions of jobs, and that Marguerite is a malfunctioning asset, not a person. His certainty is the horror. Beat: corruption as sincere arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Crew Decides
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Each crew member chooses aloud: Sefa stays, the twins stay, even knowing they'll be unpersoned. Voss confesses her academic patrons were Calloway's, and burns her credentials. Beat: found family made explicit and irreversible.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax part one: using the original's smuggled access codes, they hijack the relay's transmitter array and push the archive onto every open channel in the corridor. Calloway's marines breach as the upload completes. Beat: defiance as release.

chapters.title: Kestrel Ascending
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Climax part two: a running battle through the relay's docking spine. ORBIT sacrifices its remaining core to burn a launch corridor; the crew escapes in the jump window's final minutes as the fleet closes. Beat: cost measured in sparks and silence.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unregistered
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Adrift beyond the corridor, stripped of registry and assets, the Kestrel is now a ghost ship — like the Ashkari once were. The colony's survivors begin transmitting openly; other ships start answering. Beat: loss transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: The Name We Keep
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Calloway, exposed by the broadcast, faces his board; he sends one last message offering Marguerite reinstatement. Marguerite declines — not with anger but with a recording of the children singing. Beat: quiet victory over the arithmetic of power.

chapters.title: Orbit
chapters.summary: ORBIT's POV, reborn in a rebuilt core. The Kestrel takes a new contract: ferrying Ashkari archivists to reconnect the silent worlds. Marguerite keeps the name Hartwell, but as something chosen, not inherited. Final beat: memory kept alive by those who carry it together.
